in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have one child, Alex, who's 5 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know that Alex is 5 years old and lives with you in the UK.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I need to ask: Are you responsible for Alex's care? This typically means you're the one providing for their daily needs such as food, clothes, and their general upbringing.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for Alex - I look after them every day, provide all their meals, buy their clothes, and take care of everything they need.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that.

Now I need to ask about your residency status: Do you currently live in the UK? And if so, what is your immigration or residency status (for example, are you a UK citizen, do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another type of visa)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm a UK citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for providing that information.

Based on what you've told me:
- You have one child, Alex, who is 5 years old
- Alex lives with you in the UK
- You are responsible for Alex's care and provide for all their needs
- You are a UK citizen living in the UK

This means you meet the basic eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. Let me just confirm one final thing: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? (Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 5 years old (under 16), which meets the age requirement
- You live with Alex and are responsible for their care
- You provide for all of Alex's needs (food, clothes, etc.)
- You are a UK citizen living in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You can now proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit. If you haven't already applied, you'll need to complete a Child Benefit claim form. 

Please note: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
